context: A uni student interviews a retired bureaucrat about reforms
purpose: Teach: 弾圧/路上/戦場/破産/検察官/審理/通産省/外相

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 本日はお時間をいただきありがとうございます。まず、旧通産省での改革について伺いたいのですが。
lines.en: Thank you for your time today. First, I'd like to ask about the reforms at the former MITI.
lines.style: Polite student opening, respectful and formal tone.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ああ、懐かしいねえ。当時は労使の対立が激しくて、毎日が戦場のようだったよ。
lines.en: Ah, that brings back memories. Back then labor-management conflicts were fierce, every day felt like a battlefield.
lines.style: Nostalgic elder reflecting with warm gravitas.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 戦後の言論弾圧の名残もあった時代ですよね。デモ隊が路上に溢れたとも聞きました。
lines.en: It was an era still shadowed by postwar suppression of speech, right? I heard protesters flooded the streets.
lines.style: Curious student probing historical context carefully.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: そうそう、連日のように抗議があってね。中小企業が次々と破産していくのを止められなかった。
lines.en: Yes, protests happened day after day. We couldn't stop small businesses from going bankrupt one after another.
lines.style: Somber recollection with measured regret throughout.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 当時の外相とも調整されたと聞きますが、商法改正にも関わられたのですか?
lines.en: I heard you coordinated with the foreign minister at the time — were you also involved in commercial law reform?
lines.style: Focused follow-up question, academically inquisitive tone.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ええ、検察官や裁判所の審理にまで及ぶ案件もあってね。任命された当初は本当に大変だった。
lines.en: Yes, some cases extended to prosecutors and court hearings. The early days after my appointment were truly tough.
lines.style: Weighty elder testimony, deliberate and reflective.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 貴重なお話、本当にありがとうございます。後日、単行本にまとめさせていただければ幸いです。
lines.en: Thank you sincerely for these invaluable stories. I'd be honored to compile them into a book later.
lines.style: Grateful closing, humble and formally appreciative.
